column8: Thu 19 Nov: store, dry wit at most once in 3f: Quinion confirms cop out first meant pleading guilty, especially to a lesser charge (1930s), and evading an issue only from the 1960s; decoration on a teammate's word, so never a rebuttal of Darren and followed at once by where he was right.

Thu 19 Nov: 3f, Darren's case at its strongest, in the team's words with no outside name (none in 3f): VT rides free on other people's research, and for $29,594 that carries no stated figure the free ride is the point; Grossman and Stiglitz to References; told as what we understand now, never as the reply on 5 Oct.
Thu 19 Nov: same paper and point as row 2 (the free ride limits itself); her size moving no price is half a clause there.
Thu 19 Nov: store: US index funds passed active funds at end 2023 ($13.3tn against $13.2tn), Morningstar data read only in a news report; a dated concession clause at most, US funds only.
Thu 19 Nov: store: Bernstein's 2016 note (worse than Marxism) is the charge at its loudest, read only as reported and written by a seller of active management; never in 3f.

Thu 19 Nov: store: Pedersen shows even passive investors must trade (7.6% a year, 1926-2015; check whether 5.3 is points of the 7.6 before printing); VT's own turnover is Q117-011's; the plan makes no VT trade until the 2031 move.

Thu 19 Nov: 3f, where Darren was right, one clause with no name: pickers as a group can add a modest amount before fees, and finding one who beats the market after fees is difficult; Pedersen 2018 to References; pairs with row 2.
Thu 19 Nov: store and References: Sharpe's sum begins by selecting a market, so not picking is still a pick; adds only the first step to Q46-004.
Thu 19 Nov: the inversion (owning everything is the only sure way to own the few winners) is already RANKING_4 section 3 reason 2 on Q46-002's Bessembinder figures.
Thu 19 Nov: VT as the one published opinion is Q46-001's checkable top; its weights repeat H9-103, Q117-011 and Q136-027, printed only with 30 Sep 2026 and never beside her career.
Thu 19 Nov: store and References: Keynes ch. 12 read at source; the fail-conventionally line is already H1-048 and the beauty contest is textbook; no outside names in 3f.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c or store, skill exists: fix before use: 15.97% against 10.37% are arithmetic means against the equal-weighted DMS 100 index (re-read at source today), behind in 6 of 25 years; never the JEP's 8 points, never compound; no Keynes in 3f.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c store with row 14: Keynes's first method left him 12.6% behind by 1930 before his picks worked; a college had no date, while Laura names her top three years after VT is bought, so Darren's case is honoured and the answer is a date.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c (a top resting on picks could not be named three years ahead), the card's best figure for Laura: fix the arithmetic: Keynes's 1926-27 was a 1.42% gain against the index's 26.30%; on the card's flat-market reading the moved half loses $4,565 and the top about $4,860 (payout factor and 0.5% cut), to about $112,280, not $112,577; the step to $110,000 holds but comes from the top sitting $2,142 above $115,000, so say the dollars.
Thu 19 Nov: References and store: Hayek's knowledge of time and place, read at source, is row 17's source; no outside names in 3f.
Thu 19 Nov: the price does the work so the team spends its knowledge on Laura is row 17's point; Hayek's economy-of-knowledge line goes with row 15 to References.

Thu 19 Nov: 3f's after, in the team's words with no outside name: picking names two acts, matching her ten dates, which no price contains (IPS l.13), and forecasting companies, which the team declined; never sounds like stock picking, credits no student, counts per the IPS, said as what we understand now, never as the 5 Oct reply.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c with row 19 (its one outside name): the famous index bet held its $1 million prize in Treasury bonds bought for $318,250 a side (2017 letter, re-read today); say Treasury bonds, never strips, and only the prize maps to Laura, since the bet itself was a wager, not money held.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c aha (why the top moves before it is named): in 2012 the prize went into Berkshire shares only once Buffett agreed to make up any shortfall (re-read today), and Laura's move runs the other way; fix: the stated figure rests on IPS l.15 (money you already own), since l.11's anybody else's money covers the payments only; the switch was a valuation call and its result is never evidence.
Thu 19 Nov: same 2012 switch as row 19; brilliance wasn't needed is that row's detail, and where Darren was right (picks are affordable above a floor someone guarantees) is one clause there.
Thu 19 Nov: store: the bet's result (index 125.8%, funds of funds 2.8% to 87.7%, all five ahead in 2008 only) shows a short window can flatter picks; a market result, never evidence for Laura's plan.
Thu 19 Nov: store: Protégé's argument is Darren's case in professional form, but the card's Sources read Long Bets only as excerpted in search, so S 3; no outside names in 3f.

Thu 19 Nov: store, pedigree: Buffett's look-unimaginative line sits in the letter's lesson on waiting out irrational markets, not on index funds, so never the copout's moral; IPS l.17's rule against activity already has Q6d-029.
Thu 19 Nov: store, row 25's source: Galton's 787 guesses, middle 1,207 lb against 1,198 lb, read at source; the crowd's accuracy is well known.

Thu 19 Nov: 2.0 or 3c reserve for the one pencil image (why VT is owned but pencil, Q157-042): fix: Graham's market as a weighing machine in the long run is what a finance judge hears, so test it cold; for the funds the weighing day is a scheduled end, not a printed date (IBTA ended 15 days early), and a fund pays its net asset value.

Thu 19 Nov: References and store: Cowles 1933, the first statistical test of forecasters, read at source; drop the clause on the crash its author failed to foresee, which the card did not read at source.

Thu 19 Nov: store, 2.3 reserve: Cowles's 20 fire insurers picking shares for reserves held against claims trailed the market by 1.20% a year, 1928-31; a contrast only, since Laura's promised money holds no shares; four years, twenty firms.
Thu 19 Nov: Ellis 1975 is Q137-001 and Q46-008; the 80% of points lost, the 70% institutional share and the index line add detail there.

Thu 19 Nov: store: Bogle's folly raised $11.3m against $150m and was called a sure path to mediocrity (Zweig 2016), so the charge is fifty years old; Leuthold's poster unread, so say critics, never a named one.
Thu 19 Nov: store: Samuelson's 1974 call for a foundation to track the S&P 500 was read only as quoted; read the 1974 article and the 1976 column at source before any use; a foundation is not Laura.

Thu 19 Nov: 3f's after, one clause: over three years fees are the smallest reason for VT (about $500 against EWT, Keel arithmetic, checked) beside spread and a checkable top; fix: carry row 14's corrected loss, and Q6d-030 (RANKING_4 reason 7) already prices the choice at $800-$1,600 against luck, so use one; never call the TNA's reason wrong.
Thu 19 Nov: same idea as Q13-011 (subjective confidence is unreliable, skill in picking an illusion); the 25 advisers' .01 is a second source there; never the moral beside TNA l.23.

Thu 19 Nov: store, a dissimilar parallel for Laura the writer: Keats's negative capability is content with half knowledge, which the plan allows only in pencil; decoration unless a voice round hears it.
Thu 19 Nov: store only: Socrates knowing what he does not know is textbook and adds nothing a judge needs.
